text.headline: Timeline of Liechtenstein
text.text: Major events in the history of Liechtenstein.

events.headline: Earliest Settlements
events.text: The area now known as Liechtenstein has been inhabited since the Roman era, with evidence of settlements dating back to around 300 AD. The region was strategically important due to its location in the Alps.

events.headline: First Mention of Liechtenstein
events.text: The name 'Liechtenstein' first appeared in historical records in 1342, referring to the estate owned by the Counts of Liechtenstein. This marked the beginning of the family's influence in the region.

events.headline: Liechtenstein Becomes a Principality
events.text: In 1719, Liechtenstein was elevated to the status of a principality within the Holy Roman Empire. This formal recognition solidified the power of the Liechtenstein family in the region.

events.headline: Liechtenstein Joins the Confederation of the Rhine
events.text: Liechtenstein joined the Confederation of the Rhine, a confederation of German states under French influence, in 1806. This marked a significant shift in its political alignment during the Napoleonic Wars.

events.headline: Congress of Vienna
events.text: At the Congress of Vienna in 1815, Liechtenstein was recognized as a sovereign state. This event helped to establish its borders and political status in Europe.

events.headline: Austro-Prussian War
events.text: During the Austro-Prussian War, Liechtenstein declared neutrality and was not directly involved in the conflict. This decision allowed the principality to maintain its independence.

events.headline: New Constitution
events.text: Liechtenstein adopted a new constitution in 1921, establishing a parliamentary system and granting civil liberties. This marked a significant step towards modern governance in the principality.

events.headline: Liechtenstein's Neutrality in WWII
events.text: During World War II, Liechtenstein maintained its neutrality and avoided direct involvement in the conflict. This policy helped preserve its sovereignty and stability during a tumultuous period.

events.headline: Establishment of Diplomatic Relations
events.text: Liechtenstein established diplomatic relations with several countries, marking a new era in its foreign policy. This helped to enhance its international standing and foster economic ties.

events.headline: Liechtenstein Joins the United Nations
events.text: In 1990, Liechtenstein became a member of the United Nations, further integrating itself into the international community. This membership allowed it to participate in global discussions and initiatives.

events.headline: Constitutional Reforms
events.text: A referendum in 2003 led to constitutional reforms that increased the powers of the parliament while maintaining the prince's authority. This change reflected the evolving political landscape in Liechtenstein.

events.headline: Introduction of New Tax Laws
events.text: Liechtenstein introduced new tax laws in 2011 aimed at increasing transparency and compliance with international standards. These reforms were part of a broader effort to enhance its financial sector's reputation.

events.headline: Referendum on Monarchy
events.text: A referendum held in 2016 reaffirmed the support for the monarchy in Liechtenstein, with a significant majority voting to maintain the princely family's role. This demonstrated the public's continued trust in the monarchy.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic Response
events.text: Liechtenstein implemented measures to combat the COVID-19 pandemic, including lockdowns and vaccination campaigns. The principality's response was noted for its efficiency and effectiveness.

events.headline: 70th Anniversary of the Constitution
events.text: Liechtenstein celebrated the 70th anniversary of its constitution in 2021, reflecting on its democratic evolution and the importance of civic engagement. This milestone highlighted the principality's commitment to democratic values.

events.headline: Continued Economic Growth
events.text: Liechtenstein's economy continued to grow in 2023, driven by its financial services and manufacturing sectors. The principality remains one of the wealthiest countries in the world per capita.
